From: Asha Reddy <dpo@acme-health.com>

Subject: Staging region fallback and short-term cross-region processing Qs

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're preparing the pilot onboarding checklist and have a few specific privacy/compliance questions related to the staging environment and any transient cross-region processing that could affect our pilot data (PHI-adjacent). Can you confirm the following for the pilot:

1) Primary placement: will pilot data be stored/processed primarily in APAC (ap-southeast) for both compute and KMS-protected keys?
2) Short-term hops: our security policy allows temporary hop(s) to other regions for analytics or debugging provided: (a) explicit customer consent, (b) max duration 48 hours, and (c) full audit logs and export notice. Will Redwood accept a contract addendum to limit temporary processing to 48 hours and require notification of each event?
3) Subprocessors: please provide an initial list of subprocessors for APAC compute, analytics, and caching (include region for each). We need to vet any CDN/edge supplier (FastCache or equivalent) before onboarding.
4) Evidence: can you provide sample audit logs showing region, timestamp, and process that touched data, and confirm SOC 2 status for the relevant operators?

Attached is a short list of our DPO questions to speed review (2027-03-23_ACME_DPO_questions.pdf). We need these answers to align with our legal team for the DPA addendum.

Best,
Asha Reddy
Chief Data Protection Officer
Acme Health

--

Subject: Re: Staging region fallback and short-term cross-region processing Qs

Asha —

Thanks — really helpful list. High-level answers up front, then proposed next steps:

• Primary placement: yes — for the pilot we can provision a dedicated APAC placement (ap-southeast) for storage and primary compute. KMS keys can be bound to an APAC keystore for the pilot.

• Short-term hops: we can accept a contract-limited transient processing window. Our standard pilot offer allows transient hops for background analytics and debugging with customer consent; we propose a 48-hour maximum for the pilot (we normally cover up to 72h for certain legacy customers, but will contractually cap to 48h for Acme). Each transient event is logged and an automated notice can be sent to the customer's security contact.

• Subprocessors & evidence: Marissa and Irene are looping in the subprocessors roster and a sample audit extract. We've attached an excerpt of the DPA with the proposed pilot addendum (redwood-dpa-excerpt-v2.docx) that outlines the transient-hop clause and required notification.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to share the subprocessors roster and a sample audit extract (Irene, can you confirm retention window for pilot logs?).
2) If that looks good, we can execute a DPA addendum for the pilot and schedule a 30-min call with your cloud security lead to review the architecture.

Can you do Wednesday 24 Mar 14:00 UTC for a quick call? If not, propose two slots.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the canary dates as soon as legal confirms.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Staging region fallback and short-term cross-region processing Qs

Asha —

Appreciate the clear checklist. A few details from Legal & Ops (summary):

• Contractual commitment: we can provide a DPA addendum limited to the pilot scope (term: pilot start to pilot end). The addendum will: (a) restrict transient cross-region processing to events with customer consent, (b) cap each event at 48 hours, (c) require notification to the designated DPO/security contact within 2 hours of event start, and (d) include additional audit log fields (region, node-id, process-id).

• Subprocessors (initial roster for APAC pilot):
  - AWS (ap-southeast-2) — primary compute (managed instances)
  - Google Cloud (asia-east1) — analytics batch jobs (controlled, audited)
  - FastCache Ltd. (edge caching, ap-southeast nodes) — CDN/edge cache (we will provide contact and SLA)
  - LogStream Ops (telemetry pipeline, eu/apac-backed) — log forwarding and retention

• KMS: Keys for the pilot will be provisioned in APAC and can be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) if you prefer. We can commit in the addendum that keys used for storage encryption are provisioned in APAC unless you elect otherwise.

• Evidence & reports: we can provide a sample audit extract showing timestamped region annotations and process identifiers. SOC 2: Redwood maintains a Type II SOC 2 report covering the platform; we can share the relevant sections under an NDA.

• Retention/telemetry: pilot audit logs retained for 90 days by default; we can extend on request for longer retention in the contract.

I’ve attached the DPO questionnaire you shared and included our suggested language for the transient-hop contract clause.

If that aligns, Jordan — please confirm the canary window and we’ll prepare the DPA addendum for signature.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Ops (Privacy & Compliance) — Redwood Inference

Attachment: 2027-03-23_ACME_DPO_questions.pdf (annotated by Redwood legal)

Thanks Jordan/Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications before we lock dates: 

• FastCache — can you provide the corporate name, region mappings, and a point of contact for FastCache? We need to run a rapid vendor check.
• KMS: customer-managed keys are preferred. If we manage keys, confirm that export of plaintext keys will not occur and that any HSM operations stay in APAC.
• SOC 2 evidence: we can execute a basic NDA to receive the SOC 2 Type II relevant sections. Please send that NDA.
• Notification SLA: 2-hour notice of event start is acceptable; can you confirm that notification will include a unique event id and a link to the audit extract for that event?

Assuming the above, we can accept the 48-hour cap for pilot transient hops. We want the canary schedule and DPA addendum draft before our legal signs.

Thanks — I’ll hold the proposed window pending your confirmation.

Asha Reddy
Chief Data Protection Officer
Acme Health
